subject: Materials Science
title: Cathodic Protection: Sacrificial Anodes
description: A 60-second lesson on Cathodic Protection: Sacrificial Anodes.

hook.text: Bolt a chunk of zinc to a ship's hull and it dissolves instead of the steel — a willing sacrifice.

buildup.text: Sacrificial anode protection connects a more active metal — zinc or magnesium — to the structure.

discovery.text: The active metal becomes the anode and corrodes preferentially — keeping the steel cathodic and safe.

twist.text: Sacrificial anodes don't last forever — they must be replaced periodically as they dissolve away.

climax.text: Every ocean-going ship, offshore platform, and underground pipeline uses cathodic protection.

punchline.text: Let a cheap metal die so the expensive structure lives.

quiz.question: How does a sacrificial anode protect steel?
options: It corrodes preferentially, keeping the steel cathodic
It blocks sunlight from reaching the steel
